# Run book: Put a message on a queue

[Run books](README.md) | [User guide](../user-guide/queue-a-message.md) | [Spec](../specs/queue-a-message.md)

## Contents

- [Purpose](#purpose)

- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## Purpose

Hand work to a queue through one interface so RabbitMQ, Service Bus, Storage queues or SQS can be swapped by configuration.

## Preconditions

- RabbitMQ (or another queue adapter) is running.

## Verify

Automatically: `npx playwright test e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g "Put a message on a queue"` (add `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8088` to run against the compose stack).

By hand, in the example web application at `/messaging/queues`:

1. **Write the message.** Give the message input text and optional JSON data. Expect: The Enqueue button is enabled once input is entered.
2. **Enqueue.** The API confirms the message was queued. The link beside the button opens the generated AsyncAPI event reference. Expect: The result says the message was queued. The event reference link points to the "all" AsyncAPI document.

## Troubleshooting

**Table 1 — Known problems**

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Queued but nothing consumes it | No consumer is running for the example queue | Check the AsyncAPI page for the channel and start a consumer |
| Connection error | The queue host is localhost inside the container | Set MessageQueue__NAME__Config__HostName to the service name |

Related framework features: OoBDev.MessageQueue; OoBDev.AsyncApi.
